title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: invoke the Researcher agent through the Work IQ API
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes planned Researcher access from documented Work IQ capabilities, billing and setup. Narrow the statement about undocumented Researcher controls to API access, and remove the misleading controls-table reference beside consumption monitoring.

claims.quote: | `If-Match` | The ETag of the spending policy. Required. |

claims.claim: Changing stored non-pay-as-you-go funding to include payAsYouGo requires a billingInstrument in the request.
claims.quote: When `billingMethods` changes stored funding from non-pay-as-you-go to a value that includes `payAsYouGo`, including `prepaidCredits,payAsYouGo`, also supply a billingInstrument

claims.claim: The required billingInstrument must include billingSubscriptionId, billingResourceGroup and billingRegion.
claims.quote: with all three writable coordinates: `billingSubscriptionId`, `billingResourceGroup`, and `billingRegion`.

claims.claim: billingRegion uses a supported billing-geography key such as UnitedStates rather than an arbitrary Azure region.
claims.quote: Use a supported billing-geography key such as `UnitedStates`, not an arbitrary Azure region name.

select **Entra ID**, and then select **App registrations**.

claims.claim: Learn documents no control specific to Researcher, in the context of this planned Work IQ access.
claims.quote: Searched: "Researcher" agent admin controls block API Work IQ default. Read agent-actions, Work IQ API overview and A2A quickstart. Researcher tenant blocking is documented for Copilot, but its effect on Researcher API invocation is not stated.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn documents no control specific to Researcher' with 'Learn does not yet document a control specific to Researcher access through Work IQ'. This keeps the API qualification explicit; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions documents tenant-wide Researcher blocking in Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: In parent/child multitenant organisations, the access-token issuer must match the signed-in user's tenant.

claims.claim: The app must be registered as multitenant for that cross-tenant scenario.
claims.quote: Register the app as multitenant (`AzureADMultipleOrgs`) and have users sign in through their home tenant's authority.
